title: The case side of an outbound file outcome leaves the delivery-event element names, the route state to resume, the task code and due date, the fate of the legacy in-process interfaces and the two lake extracts unspecified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-007 (04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 007 Integration adapters for file loads and outbound files v1.md, sections 1, 3, 4, 5, 9, 11, 12, 15); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P3 Case and workflow v4.md A2.3 (route state on the case); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P2 Integration v3.md A2.1 (outbound items in the exception queue over one day: zero); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P2 Integration v3.md T3.1, T3.2 (outbound_item status list LOV-OUTBOUND-STATUS) and T-A (admin outbound-item operations); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P3 Case and workflow v3.md T3.1 (recovery_case.route_state, task, reference_row); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slide 8 (the recovery.v_ace_* views granted to rwb-source-data alone; INT-19 and INT-20 removed), slide 13 and slide 16 (P2 owns the interface row, the file run and the outbound item), slide 41 (P3 owns case, CMMN state, queues, tasks, allocation, timers) and slide 44 (JOB-13 and JOB-15 retired with the lake); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md slide 14 (workflow kit, durable timers); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (interface_config, outbound_item and job_catalog owner P2; recovery_case, task, reference_row and reference_version owner P3); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (legacy RWB-E1-007, slice RWB-P3-E1007-APP, acs []); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md R5.5 DP-03, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-11, DP-16 and DP-17 and R7.3
section: 1 Story; 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 9 State transitions; 11 Data; 12.4 Events consumed; 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story moved a case through its route states from a file outcome through the in-process interfaces CaseEvents.raise and TaskApi.raiseTask, on one recovery schema, with one retry ladder and one exception queue inside the same process, and it built the two extracts that fed the data lake. The target splits that into rwb-integration (the build, the MFT/SFTP transport, the retry intervals, the exception queue, the two outcomes FileDelivered and FileFailed) and rwb-case (the route state, the owner task, the decision record), and five values of the seam are fixed by no source read. (1) The element names of FileFailed and FileDelivered beyond the AsyncAPI document of RWB-P2-E1007-CON are not stated, and the reader needs the file, interface, business date and case set from them. (2) The carrier of the route state to resume on a later delivery is not stated: the legacy table names RESUME_STATE but no target source says where the state the case held before the move is kept, and this story reads it from the from-route-state element of the latest decision-record entry of the case and interface. (3) The task code, the element type, the owner-role rule and the due date rule of the outbound-file failure task are not stated, and the per-service login name is not stated. (4) The legacy published interfaces CaseEvents.raise and TaskApi.raiseTask and the legacy /api/recovery/v1 case-action path have no operation in the target case contract, so the move is an internal service of the listener and no path is added. (5) DP-17 removes the data lake, so JOB-15 Reporting extract (INT-19) and JOB-13 Decision log copy (INT-20) have no target home and no consumer that was not the lake; the reconciliation and the reporting of those facts move to events into rwb-reporting. The plan also allocates no legacy acceptance criterion of RWB-E1-007 to any slice (acs [] on the slice), so AC1 to AC7 have no owning new story and this slice writes eight new criteria.
evidence: split_plan.json: RWB-E1-007 slices carry acs []. Legacy section 9 names the transitions SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE to RETRY_QUEUE, RETRY_SUCCEEDED to RESUME_STATE, RETRY_LIMIT_REACHED to EXCEPTION_QUEUE, and section 12 names CaseEvents.raise, TaskApi.raiseTask and /api/recovery/v1. Legacy section 4 step 10 and section 12 name JOB-15 Reporting extract (INT-19) and JOB-13 Decision log copy (INT-20) as the outbound extracts of the module. Architecture v5 slide 8 removes INT-19 and INT-20 and grants the recovery.v_ace_* views to rwb-source-data alone; slide 44 retires JOB-13 and JOB-15. TSD P2 v3 T-A gives the admin outbound-item operations and no delivery-event payload; no source read names the task code, the due date rule or the rwb_case login.
proposed: Keep the seam as stated: the two outcomes and the admin item read from RWB-P2-E1007-CON, the route state to resume read from the latest decision-record entry of the case and interface, the task code and due date as reference rows of rwb-case, the legacy in-process interfaces as internal services of the listener with no new path, and the two lake extracts dropped under DP-17 with reporting reading rwb.case.events.v1 in rwb-reporting.

title: The rwb-case slice of RWB-E1-011 leaves the check codes, the four operation paths, the call type to rwb-source-data, the case key columns, the Schedule cron, the access right, the login and every report value that only the data lake held unspecified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-011 (04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 011 Reconciliation and data quality report v1.md, sections 3, 4, 7, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 16); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3.md A2.2, A2.11, A2.12 and A2.18; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P3 Case and workflow v4.md line 157, AC-EXC-P3-027-03, AC-EXC-P3-035-01 and A2.18; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P3 Case and workflow v3.md T3.1 (case_account DF-CAS-026, case_party DF-CAS-032, case_entry_exclusion DF-CAS-056 to DF-CAS-061, queue_member DF-WRK-045 to DF-WRK-052, assignment DF-WRK-009 to DF-WRK-016) and API-P3-001 to API-P3-027; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3.md T3.1 (reconciliation_result DF-OPS-118 to DF-OPS-129, case_list_row DF-RPT-002 to DF-RPT-019); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 13 (connection matrix, P3 to P1 is Temporal and events), 15, 29, 37, 41 and 44 (JOB-04); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (reconciliation_result and case_list_row P1; recovery_case, queue, queue_member, queue_measure, assignment, task, case_account, case_party, case_entry_exclusion P3); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (slice RWB-P3-E1011-APP, acs [], H [], C [], lane L-P3-D); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md R5.5 DP-01, DP-03, DP-05 to DP-07, DP-10, DP-11, DP-14, DP-15, DP-17 and DP-19, R5.7 and R7.3
section: 1 Story; 2 Business rationale; 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 9 State transitions; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.6 Schedules; 12.7 Tables owned; 13 Solution plan; 18 Traceability; 19 Out of scope
description: Ten values of this secondary slice are not in the sources. (1) The plan allocates no legacy acceptance criterion of RWB-E1-011 to any slice: all seven slices carry acs [], so AC1 to AC8 have no owning new story here and this slice writes ten new criteria; the legacy criteria are carried by RWB-P1-E1011-APP and RWB-ITG-E1011-ITG. (2) The three check codes and names (REC-01 EXCL, REC-05 KEY, REC-05 REF), the four run state names (TRUSTED, HELD, NOT_RUN, FAILED) and the four operation paths and their element names are this slice's design; no source names a quality run record, a result read, a facts read or a keys read for rwb-case, and the legacy story names only a job listing and two lake extracts. (3) The call type to rwb-source-data is a conflict: Architecture v5 slide 13 gives the P3 row a Temporal and event cell for P1 and no REST cell, while Template and Rules R5.5 DP-11 and the sibling slices of the key use the published REST reads of P1's data-product operations; this story follows DP-11 and P1's published API and does not use P1's bulk snapshot activity. (4) The case key columns are a conflict: FSD P3 v4 (re-based under D-RCV-35) and the legacy story name account_key, person_key and primary_person_key as ACE business keys with no foreign key, while TSD P3 v3 declares the same columns as uuid cross-references named account_id (DF-CAS-026, DF-CAS-032, DF-CAS-057) and party_id. (5) The cron of the daily quality Schedule is not stated, and neither is the time of day at which it must follow the DP01 and DP02 window of 08:00. (6) The Platform administration right of the two quality reads and of the two facts reads is not in the TSD P3 v3 rights matrix, which declares that area for the workflow smoke operation only; the legacy story's right is kept by the fill order. (7) Every report value that only the data lake held has no target: the two CSV extracts, the lake path of the date, the previous released lake date that a held publish kept, and the 07:30 Power BI data set (DP-17, ADR-018). (8) The three new quality tables carry no field ID in the Logical Data Model or the TSD. (9) The name, grants and secret reference of the rwb-case login are not in the sources. (10) The uniqueness and timeliness measures of FSD P1 v3 A2.12 are not computed by this run, and no source says which story does.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-011 section 12 names a job step, a published interface excludedAccountsByProduct(businessDate), a job listing GET /admin/jobs?type=JOB-04, a Power BI report and two extracts reconciliation/<businessDate>.csv and data-quality/<businessDate>.csv written through INT-19; section 13 names V0001 and the feature flag rwb.p1.reconciliation; section 10 names Platform administration R and Reporting R. FSD P1 v3 A2.11 gives REC-01, REC-02 and REC-05 with 'zero unexplained' and 'zero orphans; every one listed'; A2.12 gives the six measures and the 07:30 refresh from the data quality extract. FSD P3 v4 line 157 states that reconciliation of the case list to v_ace_account is reconciliation_result (JOB-04) and that a business key with no ACE row is listed by REC-05; AC-EXC-P3-035-01 names the check 'References'. TSD P3 v3 T3.1 declares account_id and party_id as uuid CROSS_REF; the FSD P3 v4 re-base note of 15 November 2026 declares account_key, person_key and case_list_row.account_key as business keys with no foreign key. Architecture v5 slide 13 gives the P3 row 'T E' for the P1 column and no R; slide 41 gives P1 the reconciliation and P3 the case, queues, tasks, allocation and timers; slide 44 gives JOB-04 to rwb-source-data; slide 29 gives the 30 views to rwb-source-data alone. ownership.json gives reconciliation_result and case_list_row to P1 and the case, exclusion, queue, membership, assignment and quality tables to P3. split_plan.json carries acs [] on every slice of RWB-E1-011.
owner_role: Solution architect, with the P1 rwb-source-data owner, the P3 rwb-case owner and the data architect
proposed: Confirm the three check codes and names and the four state names in the P3 story review; publish the four operation paths in the rwb-case service contract before the wave-1 contract test; agree with the P1 owner whether the data-product reads of this service are REST reads or P1 Temporal activities and record the answer in the service contract catalog; have the data architect decide account_id against account_key and align TSD P3 with the FSD P3 v4 re-base; set the Schedule cron with the platform workflow owner so it follows the 08:00 window; add the Platform administration right for the two quality reads to the TSD P3 rights matrix at its next version; record in the P9 reporting contract that no extract, data set or lake path exists and that the report reads the facts of this service; allocate field IDs for case_quality_run, case_quality_result and case_quality_break and for the case key columns at the next Logical Data Model version; and let the platform DB story name the rwb-case login.

title: The case side of the retention closure leaves the retention period, the retention timer type, the S7 contract element names, the route-set state names, the closure reason and the screen field names unspecified
source: RWB-E6-025 (04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md, heading RWB-E6-025); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md R-WO-36, R-WO-47 and R-WO-48; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P3 Case and workflow v3.md T2.3, T2.4, T3.1 (DF-CAS-006, DF-CAS-022, DF-CAS-023), T3.2 (LOV-TIMER, LOV-CLOSURE, LOV-STAGE), T5.3 and T-A.1; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P3 Case and workflow v4.md AC-EXC-P3-050-03; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4.md REQ-S7-008 and NFR-031 (open under DL26); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md BR-057, RULE-022 and Q-012; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 14, 20, 41 and 44 (JOB-05 retired, JOB-17 to rwb-document); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md slides 12, 13 and 28; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (document and retention_rule P5; recovery_case, task and timer P3); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (slice RWB-P3-E6025-APP, acs []); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md R5.5 DP-03, DP-13 and DP-19 and R7.3
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria; 9 State transitions; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.6 Schedules; 12.8 Contract fakes; 13 Solution plan; 15 Screens and states; 18 Traceability
description: Six values of this slice are not in the sources. (1) The retention period length is not set: NFR-031 states the period as open under DL26 and the Epics 3 to 8 requirements ask for it as question Q-012, so the story reads it as a parameter row and proves the relationship and never a value. (2) LOV-TIMER holds nine timer types and none of them is a retention timer. (3) The transport and the element names of the two write-off answers are not stated; they belong to RWB-S7-E6025-CON. (4) The three from-state and to-state names of R-WO-36, R-WO-47 and R-WO-48 (PLACED_WITH_AGENCY, RETENTION_RUNNING, CASE_CLOSED) are not values of LOV-STAGE, which lists the route stages RESTRUCTURE to DEVIATIONS, and no source states the mapping to a case stage code. (5) The closure reason column DF-CAS-023 offers eight LOV-CLOSURE values and the feature names none of them. (6) The SCR-27 field order, its masking and its merge order, and the spelling of the two new Case elements, are not stated. The plan also allocates no legacy acceptance criterion to this slice (acs []), so its eight criteria are new.
evidence: Program requirements: NFR-031 Case records carry a retention and archive rule by record class, and a case closes after its retention period, with the value Not set and the item Open under DL26; Q-012 asks what the retention periods and masking rules are by record class. TSD P3 v3 T3.2: LOV-TIMER is SERVICE_LEVEL, NOTICE_PERIOD, CURE_PERIOD, PRESCRIPTION, HEARING_DEADLINE, OFFER_VALIDITY, HOLDING_AGE, CLAIM_DEADLINE and INSTALLMENT_DUE; LOV-STAGE is RESTRUCTURE, SETTLEMENT, DEED_IN_LIEU, GUARANTEE_CLAIM, LITIGATION, ASSET_DISPOSAL, DEBT_SALE, WRITE_OFF and DEVIATIONS; LOV-CLOSURE is CURED, SETTLED, REALIZED, SOLD, WRITTEN_OFF, INSURANCE_SETTLED, MERGED and CANCELED; DF-CAS-022 closed_date and DF-CAS-023 closure_reason exist with no feature value named. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 gives R-WO-36, R-WO-47 and R-WO-48 with their from-state, event and to-state only, and no period, no timer type and no contract. split_plan.json: RWB-P3-E6025-APP carries acs []. The legacy story lists two endpoints, both of them the write-off service operations, and carries no requirement ID.
owner_role: Tech lead, with the rwb-writeoff contract owner and the rwb-case reference-data owner (RW-COE)
proposed: Hold all six as data, contract or design values: the retention period as a parameter row per product group under DL26, the retention timer type added to LOV-TIMER, the two S7 operations and their element names in RWB-S7-E6025-CON, the route-set state names written to stage_code as the rules name them, WRITTEN_OFF of LOV-CLOSURE for a retention closure, and the SCR-27 field order with the two Case element names at edge and design review; rename in this story without changing a value, a rule or a test if they differ.
